implementation_notes: kotlinx-datetime ships both halves: LocalDate (a calendar date without time or zone) and LocalDateRange, which implements ClosedRange<LocalDate> and OpenEndRange<LocalDate>, so `asOf in effective` and the rangeTo/rangeUntil operators (`..`, `..<`) work with ordinary Kotlin syntax and the bound convention is explicit at the construction site. DatePeriod and LocalDate.periodUntil cover duration questions, and the library is multiplatform, so the same domain type compiles for JVM, JS and Native. The JVM-only variant remains when the module must not take the dependency; kotlinx-datetime's LocalDate is not java.time.LocalDate, so conversions (toJavaLocalDate) belong at the boundary.
pitfalls: `..` builds a closed range and `..<` a half-open one: mixing the two conventions double-counts the changeover day, and both are valid LocalDateRange values.
An inverted range is empty rather than an error, so a swapped pair of bounds answers "not effective" for every date instead of failing fast.
kotlinx-datetime types are not java.time types: an accidental mix compiles into explicit conversions at the boundary (or fails), and comparisons across the two families are not interchangeable.

variants.name: JVM-only java.time.LocalDate bounds
variants.implementation_notes: On the JVM kotlinx-datetime delegates to java.time anyway, so the dependency can be dropped: hold java.time.LocalDate bounds (null for "until further notice"), compare with the Comparable methods, and write the overlap helper yourself - or add ThreeTen-Extra's LocalDateRange when the abuts/overlaps set is wanted. Choose this variant when the module is JVM-only and already uses the JDK date API; the kotlinx-datetime range stays the better default as soon as the code must also compile for JS or Native.
variants.idiom_name: java.time.LocalDate data class with a nullable end (JVM target only)
variants.code_sketch:
import java.time.LocalDate

data class Effectivity(val from: LocalDate, val until: LocalDate?) {   // until == null -> open
    fun contains(asOf: LocalDate): Boolean = asOf >= from && (until == null || asOf < until)
}
pitfalls: java.time.LocalDate has no range type, so `from..until` does not compile without an explicit rangeTo extension: the half-open decision has to be made in your own helper rather than inherited from a library.
A nullable until spreads null checks through every predicate; one missed check makes open-ended periods never match.

LocalDate is a value-based class: identity comparison or synchronisation on it is undefined behaviour, and equality must go through equals (which Kotlin's == does correctly for data classes but not for raw LocalDate in a lambda that uses ===).
